title: Warframe
provenance: verified locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.9.3. Also reported by Roses097 (highball-db#83, 2026-09-16), Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.9.19, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r3, rated 5 of 5 after 40 minutes, mode not stated. Mateu6 (highball-db#308, 2026-10-04), Apple M3 Pro, macOS 27.2 as written, Highball 0.10.4 (the beta), D3DMetal, engine written as x64-sikarugir10.0_6-20, which matches no engine id (r19 is the default there and r20 the macOS 27 D3DMetal 4 engine), rated 5 of 5 across every planet and environment with HDR on, no session length or recipe list given. TheCodeDaniel (highball-db#323, 2026-10-05), Apple M3 Max, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.10.3, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r19, DXMT, with the warframe and controller recipes, rated 5 of 5 after a one-minute session. vedbhoskar (highball-db#831, 2026-10-30), Apple M4, macOS 26.3, Highball 0.10.22, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, DXMT with the environment in D3DMetal mode, rated 5 of 5 after 51 minutes.
notes: Re-verified on engine r2 on 2026-09-10: the launcher updates and starts the game, Login with Steam signs in without typing anything, and the Orbiter runs at 82-94 fps at 1728x1117 fullscreen on DXMT 0.80. Apply the warframe recipe first: it turns DirectWrite off for the game's launcher only (Tools\Launcher.exe), whose embedded browser otherwise paints a black window on this engine, the same DirectWrite problem as Sikarugir #255. With that override the launcher shows its EULA, updates the game and starts it. The game itself needs nothing. Use DXMT: the first tutorial mission, with combat, ran at about 35 fps at 1728x1117 borderless (the game's own low preset, 1280x720 render, anti-aliasing and ambient occlusion off) with the Metal HUD reading 28 ms of GPU per frame; later in the same session, past the tutorial, the maintainer's own play ran above 100 fps by the HUD. DXVK also reaches the mission but is GPU-bound at about 16 fps (51 ms GPU) with the same settings. 'Login with Steam' works; a Steam account without a Warframe account gets the game's own bind-or-create dialog, which is normal. A sleeping display stalls the game for as long as it sleeps, so keep the Mac awake for long sessions. Verified 2026-09-04 on macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro: launcher update, Steam login, account creation, tutorial mission and later play; Exit Game shuts the process down cleanly (the game log ends with its normal shutdown). A D3DMetal report on the 0.10.4 beta on an M3 Pro with macOS 27 rates it perfect across every planet and environment with HDR on, with a frame rate drop in Duviri that the reporter says every platform shows. Which engine ran it is not settled, the id in the report matches none, and on macOS 27 D3DMetal is 3.0 on the default r19 or 4.0 beta 2 on the opt-in r20. No frame rate was given for that session. The anti-cheat map still lists Warframe with a custom anti-cheat and a warning verdict, and this reporter, like the earlier ones, played without a kick.

anticheat.note: anti-cheat present; Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS — userspace path works for some titles

dxmt.detail: re-verified on engine r2 2026-09-10: signed in with the Login with Steam button, reached the Orbiter with live chat and the Vor's Prize objective, 82-94 fps at 1728x1117 fullscreen with 12.0-12.4 ms of GPU per frame, DXMT 0.80 (macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro). The launcher reports up to date and its Play button works. On r1 the tutorial mission ran at about 35 fps with 28 ms GPU per frame and above 100 fps later in that session (2026-09-04)

dxvk.detail: reaches the same mission but GPU-bound at about 16 fps, 51 ms GPU per frame, same settings

knownIssues.symptom: Frame rate drops in Duviri (reported on an M3 Pro, D3DMetal, Highball 0.10.4 beta, highball-db#308)
knownIssues.cause: Not investigated here. The reporter says the same drop happens on every platform
